Introduction Opening frame for **Tools** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biotechnology — Principles and Processes fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Genetic engineering needs a standard toolkit. **Restriction enzymes** — the molecular scissors — recognise specific palindromic sequences and cut, leaving sticky or blunt ends. **Vectors** — plasmids, phage, cosmids — carry the gene into cells and replicate there; they need an origin of replication, a selectable marker and cloning sites. rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Restriction enzymes: cut palindromic sites; EcoRI = E. coli restriction I; produce sticky ends (5' overhangs) — the nomenclature and sticky ends are the marks.  ·  Trick 2: Vector requirements: origin of replication (ori), selectable marker (antibiotic resistance), cloning site (MCS), small size, high copy number — five criteria.

The gene is inserted at a site inside tetR. Cells grown on ampicillin survive if they carry any plasmid; cells grown on tetracycline die if the insert disrupted tetR. So the clone of interest is: ampicillin-resistant AND tetracycline-sensitive.…
